item.vignette: A kinase preparation containing TYK2 is exposed to deucravacitinib. Structural analysis shows binding outside the catalytic ATP-binding site, and receptor-mediated STAT phosphorylation falls. Increasing ATP concentration does not reverse the inhibitory interaction.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains these findings?

options.A: Binding the TYK2 regulatory domain and stabilizing an inhibitory interaction with its catalytic domain
options.B: Competing with ATP at the catalytic site of JAK1
options.D: Promoting proteasomal degradation of STAT proteins
options.E: Irreversibly modifying the TYK2 catalytic cysteine

item.tested_construct: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition through the regulatory domain
item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing regulatory-domain allostery from ATP-site JAK inhibition and extracellular cytokine neutralization.

explanation.key_explanation: Deucravacitinib binds the regulatory domain of TYK2 and stabilizes an inhibitory interaction between the regulatory and catalytic domains, producing allosteric inhibition of TYK2 activation and downstream STAT signaling.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Regulatory-domain binding explains non-ATP-competitive TYK2 inhibition.
distractor_explanations.B: The observed binding site is not the JAK1 catalytic ATP pocket.
distractor_explanations.C: IL-23 neutralization is extracellular and would not explain direct binding to purified TYK2.
distractor_explanations.D: STAT degradation is not the documented direct mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: The label describes regulatory-domain allostery, not irreversible covalent catalytic-site inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish allosteric regulatory-domain kinase inhibition from ATP-competitive inhibition.

sources.title: SOTYKTU- deucravacitinib tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: ATP-site JAK inhibition is plausible pharmacologically but is excluded by the regulatory-domain structural result and ATP-independence.

item.vignette: Human neutrophils are exposed to a fixed concentration of C5a. Avacopan reduces C5a-induced CD11b upregulation and chemotaxis, but a separate cell-free assay shows that C5 can still be cleaved and terminal complement components can form.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains this pattern?

options.B: Antagonism of the C5a receptor on neutrophils
options.D: Binding of C3 to prevent C3 convertase formation
options.E: Inhibition of C1s in the classical pathway

item.tested_construct: C5a receptor antagonism versus complement-protein blockade
item.difficulty_basis: Requires localizing inhibition to C5a signaling rather than upstream or terminal complement generation.

explanation.key_explanation: Avacopan antagonizes the C5a receptor and blocks C5a-mediated neutrophil activation and migration without directly preventing generation of C5a/C5b by C5 cleavage.

distractor_explanations.A: C5 neutralization would alter C5 cleavage and terminal-complement formation, which remain intact in the separate assay.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. C5aR blockade explains impaired neutrophil response despite preserved complement-protein processing.
distractor_explanations.C: Factor D inhibition acts upstream in the alternative pathway and would alter complement amplification rather than selectively block neutrophil C5a sensing.
distractor_explanations.D: C3 blockade is upstream and does not match preserved complement generation with selective C5a signaling loss.
distractor_explanations.E: C1s inhibition selectively affects the classical pathway, not direct C5a receptor signaling.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish blockade of a complement receptor from inhibition of complement-protein generation.

sources.title: TAVNEOS- avacopan capsule
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: C5 blockade can reduce C5a signaling but would also alter C5 cleavage/terminal complement, which the stem preserves.

author_qa.hidden_assumptions: PASS — precise therapeutic mechanism in ANCA vasculitis is not overclaimed

item.vignette: Isolated gastric parietal-cell proton pumps are exposed to vonoprazan under conditions that do not require an acidic activation step. Pump inhibition is reversible and is reduced when potassium concentration near the enzyme is increased.
item.lead_in: Which mechanism best explains the finding?

options.A: Irreversible covalent inhibition after acid-dependent prodrug activation
options.B: Competitive blockade of the histamine H2 receptor
options.C: Potassium-competitive reversible inhibition of the gastric H+/K+-ATPase
options.D: Neutralization of secreted gastric acid in the lumen
options.E: Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in parietal cells

item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing potassium-competitive acid blockers from conventional acid-activated proton-pump inhibitors.

explanation.key_explanation: Vonoprazan inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase in a potassium-competitive, noncovalent, reversible manner and does not require acid activation.

distractor_explanations.A: This describes conventional covalent proton-pump inhibition and conflicts with reversible, acid-independent inhibition.
distractor_explanations.B: H2 blockade acts at a receptor upstream of the proton pump, not directly in the purified-pump assay.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Potassium competition, reversibility, and lack of acid activation identify vonoprazan's mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Luminal neutralization does not inhibit the isolated pump.
distractor_explanations.E: Carbonic anhydrase contributes to acid secretion but is not the documented vonoprazan target.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate potassium-competitive acid blockade from acid-activated irreversible proton-pump inhibition.

sources.title: VOQUEZNA- vonoprazan fumarate tablet
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both A and C inhibit the proton pump, but the stem explicitly supplies reversibility, potassium competition, and acid-independent action, uniquely selecting C.

item.vignette: Influenza-infected cells are exposed to the active metabolite of baloxavir marboxil. Viral polymerase can still bind RNA templates, but cleavage of host capped RNA primers used to initiate viral mRNA synthesis is blocked.
item.lead_in: Which viral function is directly inhibited?

options.C: Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase elongation at the catalytic polymerase site
options.D: Cap-dependent endonuclease activity of the polymerase acidic protein

item.difficulty_basis: Requires recognizing cap-snatching as a distinct influenza polymerase function.

explanation.key_explanation: Baloxavir inhibits the cap-dependent endonuclease activity of the influenza polymerase acidic (PA) protein, preventing cleavage of capped host RNA primers needed for viral gene transcription.

distractor_explanations.A: Neuraminidase inhibitors impair virion release, not capped-primer generation.
distractor_explanations.B: M2 blockade impairs uncoating and does not explain the transcriptional primer defect.
distractor_explanations.C: The target is the PA endonuclease function rather than the polymerase elongation catalytic site.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Loss of cap-snatching identifies PA cap-dependent endonuclease inhibition.
distractor_explanations.E: Hemagglutinin mediates attachment and does not produce capped RNA primers.

explanation.educational_objective: Localize an influenza antiviral mechanism to cap-snatching rather than entry, uncoating, elongation, or virion release.

sources.title: XOFLUZA- baloxavir marboxil tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Current DailyMed clinical-pharmacology/microbiology content checked 2026-09-08; mechanism supported in 12.4

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both concern viral RNA synthesis, but the stem specifically identifies host capped-primer cleavage, a PA endonuclease function rather than polymerase elongation.

item.vignette: Plasma from a patient with hemophilia A contains no functional factor VIII. Addition of emicizumab restores intrinsic tenase activity even though no factor VIII protein is supplied and no thrombin-mediated factor VIII activation step is required.
item.lead_in: Which interaction directly produces this effect?

options.A: Binding tissue factor and factor VIIa
options.C: Activating factor X directly without factor IXa
options.D: Replacing factor VIII with recombinant factor VIII protein
options.E: Bridging activated factor IX and factor X to mimic factor VIIIa cofactor function

item.tested_construct: Bispecific FIXa-FX bridging that substitutes for FVIIIa cofactor activity
item.difficulty_basis: Requires understanding intrinsic tenase assembly rather than simple factor replacement.

explanation.key_explanation: Emicizumab bridges activated factor IX and factor X, restoring the cofactor function normally supplied by activated factor VIII in intrinsic tenase.

distractor_explanations.A: Tissue factor/FVIIa initiates the extrinsic pathway and is not emicizumab's binding pair.
distractor_explanations.B: TFPI antagonism is a different non-factor replacement strategy.
distractor_explanations.C: Emicizumab does not directly activate FX independently of FIXa; it positions FIXa and FX.
distractor_explanations.D: No FVIII protein is supplied, and emicizumab is structurally distinct from FVIII.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Bispecific FIXa-FX bridging restores missing FVIIIa cofactor function.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize functional substitution for a coagulation cofactor through bispecific assembly of its enzyme and substrate.

sources.title: HEMLIBRA- emicizumab injection, solution
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08
sources.section_locator: 7.2 Drug-Laboratory Test Interactions; 12.1 Mechanism of Action

second_answer_attack.resolution: TFPI blockade also improves thrombin generation in hemophilia but does not recreate FVIIIa tenase cofactor activity by FIXa-FX bridging.

item.vignette: Pituitary corticotrophs are exposed to corticotropin-releasing factor in the presence of crinecerfont. ACTH secretion decreases even though CRF concentration remains unchanged. A receptor-selectivity assay shows preserved CRF type 2 receptor signaling.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains the result?

options.A: Selective antagonism of pituitary CRF type 1 receptors
options.B: Agonism of glucocorticoid receptors in corticotrophs
options.D: Antagonism of melanocortin 2 receptors in the adrenal cortex

item.tested_construct: Selective CRF1 antagonism and ACTH suppression
item.difficulty_basis: Requires localizing the drug to pituitary CRF1 rather than adrenal steroidogenesis or hypothalamic production.

explanation.key_explanation: Crinecerfont selectively antagonizes CRF type 1 receptors in the pituitary, blocking CRF-driven ACTH secretion and thereby reducing ACTH-mediated adrenal androgen production.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. The pituitary assay and preserved CRF2 signaling identify selective CRF1 antagonism.
distractor_explanations.B: Glucocorticoid receptor agonism could suppress ACTH through feedback but is not crinecerfont's direct target.
distractor_explanations.C: 21-hydroxylase inhibition is the inherited enzymatic problem in classic CAH, not the drug mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: MC2R antagonism would act in adrenal cells, which are absent from the pituitary assay.
distractor_explanations.E: CRF concentration is held constant, excluding reduced hypothalamic CRF production as the direct explanation.

explanation.educational_objective: Trace selective pituitary receptor blockade to reduced downstream adrenal stimulation.

sources.title: CRENESSITY- crinecerfont capsules/oral solution
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both CRF1 blockade and glucocorticoid feedback can suppress ACTH, but the direct receptor-selectivity assay uniquely identifies CRF1 antagonism.

item.vignette: Airway smooth-muscle and inflammatory-cell preparations are exposed to ensifentrine. Enzyme assays show reduced hydrolysis of both cAMP and, in one enzyme system, cGMP; intracellular cyclic nucleotide concentrations rise without direct beta-2 adrenergic receptor stimulation.
item.lead_in: Which enzyme pair is directly inhibited?

options.D: Adenylyl cyclase and guanylyl cyclase

item.difficulty_basis: Requires matching cyclic-nucleotide substrate profiles to two phosphodiesterase targets.

explanation.key_explanation: Ensifentrine inhibits PDE3 and PDE4. PDE3 hydrolyzes mainly cAMP but can also hydrolyze cGMP, whereas PDE4 hydrolyzes cAMP, so dual inhibition increases intracellular cyclic nucleotides.

distractor_explanations.A: PDE5 predominantly hydrolyzes cGMP and is not one of ensifentrine's labeled targets.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. The drug directly inhibits PDE3 and PDE4.
distractor_explanations.C: Neither PDE2 nor PDE5 is the documented target pair.
distractor_explanations.D: Cyclase inhibition would reduce rather than explain accumulation of cyclic nucleotides.
distractor_explanations.E: Adenylyl cyclase is not inhibited; blocking it would reduce cAMP production.

explanation.educational_objective: Use second-messenger substrate profiles to identify dual phosphodiesterase inhibition.

sources.title: OHTUVAYRE- ensifentrine inhalation suspension
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: PDE4/PDE5 could also influence cAMP/cGMP separately, but current labeling directly identifies PDE3 and PDE4 and the substrate profile fits that pair.

item.vignette: Keratinocytes carrying a reporter responsive to a ligand-activated transcription factor are exposed to tapinarof. Reporter activity increases. Investigators are instructed to identify only the directly documented receptor pharmacology and not to claim that this single pathway fully explains the drug's therapeutic actions in inflammatory skin disease.
item.lead_in: Which receptor is directly activated?

options.D: Vitamin D receptor

item.difficulty_basis: Tests nuclear/transcriptional receptor recognition and evidence-boundary discipline.

explanation.key_explanation: Tapinarof is an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist. Current labeling also states that the specific mechanisms by which it exerts therapeutic actions are unknown.

distractor_explanations.A: Glucocorticoid receptors are not the documented tapinarof target.
distractor_explanations.B: Retinoid receptors are distinct nuclear receptors and are not directly activated by tapinarof.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. AhR agonism is directly documented.
distractor_explanations.D: Vitamin D receptor activation is not the labeled pharmacology.
distractor_explanations.E: PPAR-gamma is not the documented receptor target.

explanation.educational_objective: Separate directly demonstrated receptor pharmacology from an incompletely established therapeutic mechanism.

sources.title: VTAMA- tapinarof cream
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Several transcriptional receptors affect keratinocyte biology, but only AhR is directly documented as tapinarof's receptor pharmacology.

author_qa.hidden_assumptions: PASS — specific therapeutic mechanism is explicitly not asserted

item.vignette: Brain tissue from a patient with Alzheimer disease is incubated with fluorescently labeled donanemab. Binding is concentrated over insoluble amyloid plaques enriched for an N-terminally modified amyloid-beta species rather than over soluble tau or intact amyloid precursor protein.
item.lead_in: Which antigen is the antibody designed to recognize?

options.A: Soluble monomeric amyloid-beta regardless of N-terminal processing
options.D: Insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid-beta
options.E: Amyloid precursor protein at the neuronal membrane

item.tested_construct: Donanemab antigen specificity for pyroglutamate amyloid-beta plaque
item.difficulty_basis: Requires differentiating plaque-directed antibody specificity from tau, APP, and secretase targets.

explanation.key_explanation: Donanemab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid beta and reduces amyloid-beta plaque burden.

distractor_explanations.A: The labeled target is a specific insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid-beta species rather than nonspecific soluble monomer.
distractor_explanations.B: Tau is a distinct Alzheimer pathology and is not the donanemab antigen.
distractor_explanations.C: Donanemab does not inhibit beta-secretase directly.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. The antibody recognizes insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid beta.
distractor_explanations.E: APP is the precursor protein but is not the labeled antibody target.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish direct antibody targeting of a pathologic protein species from inhibition of its upstream production pathway.

sources.title: KISUNLA- donanemab-azbt injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on cited current DailyMed 12.1 mechanism section; current page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both are amyloid-beta species, but the label specifies insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid beta and the stem localizes binding to plaques.

item.vignette: Candida cells are exposed to ibrexafungerp. Incorporation of glucose into an essential fungal cell-wall polymer falls, while ergosterol concentration and fungal ribosomal protein synthesis are initially unchanged.
item.lead_in: Which enzyme is directly inhibited?

options.D: Fungal thymidylate synthase

item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing cell-wall glucan synthesis from ergosterol and nucleic-acid targets.

explanation.key_explanation: Ibrexafungerp inhibits glucan synthase, reducing formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential fungal cell-wall component.

distractor_explanations.A: Squalene epoxidase affects ergosterol synthesis rather than glucan polymer formation.
distractor_explanations.B: Azole inhibition of 14-alpha-demethylase alters ergosterol, which is stipulated unchanged initially.
distractor_explanations.C: Chitin is a different fungal cell-wall polymer.
distractor_explanations.D: Thymidylate synthase inhibition affects DNA synthesis, not beta-glucan assembly.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Glucan synthase produces the 1,3-beta-D-glucan affected in the experiment.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate fungal cell-wall glucan inhibition from membrane-sterol and nucleic-acid mechanisms.

sources.title: BREXAFEMME- ibrexafungerp tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Current DailyMed label updated 2024-11-04 and 12.4 mechanism text checked 2026-09-08; no unsupported mechanism-section revision date asserted

second_answer_attack.resolution: Chitin synthase is also a fungal cell-wall target, but the specific 1,3-beta-D-glucan polymer uniquely identifies glucan synthase.

item.vignette: Breast-cancer cells with PTEN loss are exposed to capivasertib. Phosphorylation of several downstream AKT substrates decreases. Parallel purified-kinase assays show inhibition of AKT1, AKT2, and AKT3.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains these findings?

options.A: Inhibition of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms
options.D: Inhibition of mTORC1 without affecting AKT

item.difficulty_basis: Requires locating the intervention within PI3K-PTEN-AKT signaling rather than attributing downstream effects to upstream correction.

explanation.key_explanation: Capivasertib inhibits AKT1, AKT2, and AKT3 and thereby decreases phosphorylation of downstream AKT substrates.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Direct inhibition of all three AKT isoforms matches the purified-kinase and downstream-phosphorylation findings.
distractor_explanations.B: PI3K-alpha lies upstream and is not the direct capivasertib target.
distractor_explanations.C: PTEN loss remains present; the drug does not restore PTEN expression.
distractor_explanations.D: mTORC1 is downstream of AKT and does not explain direct inhibition of purified AKT isoforms.
distractor_explanations.E: ER-alpha degradation is a different endocrine-oncology mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Localize a pathway inhibitor using both direct kinase assays and downstream substrate phosphorylation.

sources.title: TRUQAP- capivasertib tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: PI3K inhibition could lower downstream AKT signaling but cannot explain direct inhibition of purified AKT1/2/3.

item.vignette: ER-positive breast-cancer cells are exposed to elacestrant. Estradiol-stimulated proliferation decreases and ER-alpha protein abundance falls. Adding a proteasome inhibitor attenuates the fall in receptor protein.
item.lead_in: Which direct pharmacologic action best explains these findings?

options.A: Aromatase inhibition with reduced estrogen synthesis
options.B: ER-alpha antagonism with proteasome-mediated receptor degradation
options.D: CDK4/6 inhibition causing G1 arrest independent of ER

item.tested_construct: Estrogen-receptor antagonism coupled to ER-alpha degradation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires integrating receptor antagonism with proteasome-sensitive receptor loss.

explanation.key_explanation: Elacestrant is an ER-alpha antagonist; at relevant concentrations it induces proteasome-mediated degradation of ER-alpha protein and inhibits estradiol-mediated proliferation.

distractor_explanations.A: Aromatase inhibition lowers ligand synthesis but would not directly explain proteasome-sensitive loss of ER-alpha protein in the cell assay.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. ER-alpha antagonism plus receptor degradation matches both findings.
distractor_explanations.C: Progesterone receptors are not the direct target.
distractor_explanations.D: CDK4/6 blockade can inhibit proliferation but does not explain selective ER-alpha degradation.
distractor_explanations.E: HER2 inhibition is unrelated to the receptor-protein loss described.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish ligand deprivation from direct receptor antagonism that also drives receptor degradation.

sources.title: ORSERDU- elacestrant tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 mechanism section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: CDK4/6 inhibition can reduce ER-positive tumor proliferation, but it does not explain the observed proteasome-sensitive decrease in ER-alpha protein.

item.vignette: Small-cell lung-cancer cells expressing DLL3 are cocultured with T lymphocytes. Tarlatamab promotes T-cell activation and tumor-cell lysis. Blocking either DLL3 on the tumor cell or one component of the T-cell receptor complex eliminates the effect.
item.lead_in: Which target pair is directly engaged?

options.D: DLL3 and CD28

item.difficulty_basis: Requires identifying the tumor antigen and T-cell engagement target from functional blockade experiments.

explanation.key_explanation: Tarlatamab is a bispecific T-cell engager that binds DLL3 on target cells and CD3 on T cells, activating T cells and causing lysis of DLL3-expressing cells.

distractor_explanations.A: Checkpoint blockade does not directly bridge DLL3-positive tumor cells to T cells.
distractor_explanations.B: CD3 is correct for the T-cell side, but CD20 is not the tumor antigen targeted by tarlatamab.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. DLL3 and CD3 are the documented binding pair.
distractor_explanations.D: DLL3 is correct, but the T-cell target is CD3 rather than CD28.
distractor_explanations.E: Neither target pair matches the documented bispecific engager.

explanation.educational_objective: Infer a bispecific engager's molecular targets from loss-of-function blockade on tumor and effector cells.

sources.title: IMDELLTRA- tarlatamab-dlle for injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: DLL3-CD28 could theoretically provide costimulation, but the label and T-cell-receptor-complex clue identify CD3.

item.vignette: Folate-receptor-alpha-positive ovarian-cancer cells bind an antibody-drug conjugate and internalize it. Intracellular proteolysis releases a small-molecule payload, after which mitotic spindle organization fails and cells arrest before undergoing apoptosis.
item.lead_in: Which mechanism best describes the conjugate?

options.A: HER2-directed delivery of a topoisomerase I inhibitor
options.B: FR-alpha-directed delivery of a DNA-alkylating agent
options.C: CD33-directed delivery of a ribosomal toxin
options.D: FR-alpha-directed delivery of the microtubule inhibitor DM4

item.tested_construct: FR-alpha ADC internalization and DM4-mediated microtubule disruption
item.difficulty_basis: Requires integrating antigen specificity, ADC trafficking, and payload mechanism.

explanation.key_explanation: Mirvetuximab soravtansine is an FR-alpha-directed ADC. After binding and internalization, proteolytic cleavage releases DM4, which disrupts microtubules and causes cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.

distractor_explanations.A: This describes a different ADC antigen and payload class.
distractor_explanations.B: FR-alpha is correct, but the payload is a microtubule inhibitor rather than a DNA alkylator.
distractor_explanations.C: CD33 is a myeloid antigen and does not match the ovarian-cancer target.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. FR-alpha targeting plus intracellular DM4 release explains the spindle defect.
distractor_explanations.E: PSMA radioligand therapy uses ionizing radiation rather than an intracellular microtubule payload.

explanation.educational_objective: Analyze an ADC by separately identifying its cell-surface target, internalization step, and cytotoxic payload.

sources.title: ELAHERE- mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: FR-alpha targeting alone is insufficient; the explicit spindle defect and labeled DM4 payload uniquely select D.

item.vignette: A radiolabeled small molecule accumulates in PSMA-expressing prostate-cancer cells and nearby tumor cells. Dosimetry shows short-range ionizing emissions, and DNA double-strand damage increases in the targeted region without inhibition of androgen-receptor signaling.
item.lead_in: Which direct mechanism best explains the antitumor effect?

options.A: Internalization of a microtubule toxin through PSMA
options.B: Competitive inhibition of prostate-specific membrane antigen enzymatic activity
options.C: Alpha-particle emission from radium incorporated into bone
options.D: Blockade of androgen binding to the androgen receptor
options.E: PSMA-directed delivery of lutetium-177 beta-minus radiation causing DNA damage

item.difficulty_basis: Requires separating receptor targeting from the physical cytotoxic mechanism of a radionuclide payload.

explanation.key_explanation: Lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan binds PSMA and delivers beta-minus radiation from lutetium-177 to PSMA-expressing and nearby cells, producing DNA damage that can cause cell death.

distractor_explanations.A: The payload is a radionuclide rather than a microtubule toxin.
distractor_explanations.B: PSMA binding provides targeting; inhibition of PSMA enzymatic function is not the cytotoxic mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: This is not a bone-seeking radium alpha-emitter.
distractor_explanations.D: Androgen-receptor signaling is not the direct target in this radioligand mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. PSMA targeting localizes beta-minus radiation and DNA damage.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish molecular targeting from the cytotoxic payload in radioligand therapy.

sources.title: PLUVICTO- lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: The molecule binds PSMA, but the label identifies beta-minus radiation-induced DNA damage—not PSMA enzyme inhibition—as the cytotoxic mechanism.

item.vignette: An alternative-complement-pathway assay is performed in the presence of danicopan. Cleavage of factor B into Ba and Bb decreases, formation of C3bBb falls, and C3-fragment deposition on erythrocytes is reduced.
item.lead_in: Which complement protein is directly inhibited?

options.D: Factor B

item.tested_construct: Factor-D inhibition upstream of alternative-pathway C3 convertase
item.difficulty_basis: Requires localizing an alternative-pathway enzyme from factor-B cleavage and C3-convertase assembly.

explanation.key_explanation: Danicopan reversibly binds complement factor D, preventing factor-B cleavage required for formation of the alternative-pathway C3 convertase C3bBb and downstream C3-fragment opsonization.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Factor D cleaves factor B in the alternative pathway and is directly inhibited by danicopan.
distractor_explanations.B: C5 blockade is downstream and does not directly prevent factor-B cleavage.
distractor_explanations.C: C1s is a classical-pathway protease.
distractor_explanations.D: Factor B is the substrate whose cleavage is prevented, not the direct danicopan target.
distractor_explanations.E: Properdin stabilizes C3bBb but is not the labeled target.

explanation.educational_objective: Use a blocked proteolytic step to distinguish an enzyme target from its substrate and downstream complement components.

sources.title: VOYDEYA- danicopan tablet, film coated
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Factor B is central to the observed step but is the cleavage substrate; current labeling directly identifies factor D as the inhibited enzyme.

item.vignette: Hepatocytes exposed to fitusiran show a selective decrease in antithrombin messenger RNA followed by lower antithrombin protein secretion. The antithrombin gene sequence and transcription-initiation rate remain unchanged.
item.lead_in: Which molecular process directly accounts for the effect?

options.A: CRISPR disruption of the SERPINC1 gene
options.D: Neutralization of antithrombin protein by a monoclonal antibody
options.E: Inhibition of vitamin K epoxide reductase

item.difficulty_basis: Requires localizing the intervention to post-transcriptional RNA interference rather than gene editing or protein neutralization.

explanation.key_explanation: Fitusiran is a double-stranded siRNA that drives RNA-interference-mediated degradation of antithrombin mRNA, reducing plasma antithrombin levels.

distractor_explanations.A: The gene sequence remains unchanged, excluding genome editing.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Selective mRNA loss followed by reduced protein is the labeled siRNA mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Protein degradation would not explain the preceding fall in mRNA.
distractor_explanations.D: Protein neutralization would not reduce hepatocyte antithrombin mRNA.
distractor_explanations.E: Vitamin K antagonism reduces synthesis of several clotting factors and is not antithrombin-directed.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate RNA interference from genome editing and protein-level inhibition using temporal molecular readouts.

sources.title: QFITLIA- fitusiran injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both reduce effective antithrombin, but only RNA interference explains selective antithrombin mRNA loss in hepatocytes.

item.vignette: Hemophilic plasma lacking functional factor VIII or IX is exposed to concizumab. Free tissue factor pathway inhibitor falls, factor Xa generation during the initiation phase rises, and thrombin generation improves without replacement of the missing clotting factor.
item.lead_in: Which protein is directly antagonized?

options.D: Factor Xa

item.tested_construct: TFPI antagonism that enhances initiation-phase FXa generation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing removal of an endogenous anticoagulant brake from direct factor replacement.

explanation.key_explanation: Concizumab is a monoclonal antibody antagonist of endogenous TFPI. TFPI inhibition increases FXa generation during coagulation initiation and improves thrombin generation.

distractor_explanations.A: Antithrombin reduction is the target of a different rebalancing strategy.
distractor_explanations.B: Activated protein C is not the labeled concizumab target.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Reduced free TFPI and increased initiation-phase FXa identify TFPI antagonism.
distractor_explanations.D: FXa is increased rather than inhibited by the mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Thrombomodulin is not the target.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize hemostatic rebalancing by inhibition of an endogenous anticoagulant rather than replacement of a deficient procoagulant factor.

sources.title: ALHEMO- concizumab-mtci injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Antithrombin reduction is a plausible hemophilia rebalancing mechanism, but the observed fall in free TFPI uniquely identifies concizumab's target.

item.vignette: A trigeminal-system receptor assay is performed with zavegepant. A fixed concentration of calcitonin gene-related peptide is present, but receptor-mediated signaling decreases. Serotonin-receptor binding and CGRP peptide concentration are unchanged.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains the result?

options.B: Neutralization of circulating CGRP peptide with an antibody
options.C: Inhibition of CGRP synthesis in sensory neurons
options.D: Antagonism of the CGRP receptor

item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing receptor antagonism from ligand neutralization and serotonin-receptor agonism.

explanation.key_explanation: Zavegepant is a CGRP receptor antagonist. The item is restricted to that directly documented receptor pharmacology; labeling notes that the relationship between pharmacodynamic activity and the clinical mechanism is unknown.

distractor_explanations.A: This is a triptan-like serotonin mechanism and does not match the direct CGRP-receptor assay.
distractor_explanations.B: CGRP concentration is unchanged and zavegepant is a small-molecule receptor antagonist rather than a ligand-neutralizing antibody.
distractor_explanations.C: Fixed ligand concentration excludes reduced peptide synthesis.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. CGRP-receptor antagonism explains reduced signaling with unchanged ligand concentration.
distractor_explanations.E: PAC1 is a different neuropeptide receptor.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish neuropeptide receptor antagonism from ligand neutralization and serotonin-receptor agonism.

sources.title: ZAVZPRET- zavegepant nasal spray
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 mechanism section; current page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Ligand neutralization can also reduce CGRP signaling, but the fixed peptide concentration and labeled small-molecule receptor target uniquely select D.

author_qa.hidden_assumptions: PASS — complete clinical mechanism is not asserted

item.vignette: A serotonin-receptor panel is tested with lasmiditan. High-affinity binding and agonist activity are observed at one receptor subtype, whereas the classic vasoconstrictive 5-HT1B/1D receptor pair is not the defining target in the experiment.
item.lead_in: Which receptor is directly activated?

options.D: 5-HT1B

item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing a ditan receptor subtype from triptan-associated serotonin receptors.

explanation.key_explanation: Lasmiditan binds with high affinity to and acts as an agonist at the 5-HT1F receptor. Its precise therapeutic mechanism in migraine is not fully established.

distractor_explanations.A: 5-HT2A is not the labeled high-affinity receptor target.
distractor_explanations.B: 5-HT3 is a ligand-gated ion channel and is not lasmiditan's target.
distractor_explanations.C: 5-HT1A is not the defining receptor subtype.
distractor_explanations.D: 5-HT1B is associated with triptan pharmacology; lasmiditan is defined by 5-HT1F agonism.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Lasmiditan directly activates 5-HT1F receptors.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate 5-HT1F agonism from classic 5-HT1B/1D migraine pharmacology.

sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on cited current DailyMed 12.1 mechanism section; current page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: 5-HT1B is a familiar migraine receptor, but the label directly identifies high-affinity 5-HT1F binding/agonism and the stem excludes classic 1B/1D pharmacology.

item.vignette: Growth-plate chondrocytes carrying an activating FGFR3 mutation are exposed to vosoritide. Intracellular cGMP rises and ERK1/2 activation downstream of FGFR3 decreases at the RAF-1 level, while the mutant FGFR3 sequence remains unchanged.
item.lead_in: Which direct receptor action initiates this effect?

options.B: Antagonism of FGFR3 at its extracellular ligand-binding site
options.D: Inhibition of phosphodiesterase type 5

item.difficulty_basis: Requires tracing cGMP-linked NPR-B signaling to suppression of RAF-ERK downstream of mutant FGFR3.

explanation.key_explanation: Vosoritide binds and activates NPR-B. This antagonizes FGFR3 downstream signaling by inhibiting ERK1/2 in the MAPK pathway at RAF-1, promoting endochondral bone growth.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. NPR-B activation explains the cGMP rise and antagonism of FGFR3 downstream signaling.
distractor_explanations.B: Vosoritide does not repair or directly antagonize mutant FGFR3 at its extracellular site.
distractor_explanations.C: Growth-hormone receptor signaling is not the direct target.
distractor_explanations.D: PDE5 inhibition can raise cGMP but does not match the documented receptor binding or RAF-level mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: PTH1R activation is a different skeletal/endocrine pathway.

explanation.educational_objective: Explain how activation of a cGMP-linked receptor can oppose a pathogenic receptor-tyrosine-kinase MAPK signal downstream.

sources.title: VOXZOGO- vosoritide for injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: PDE5 inhibition could increase cGMP, but the label specifically identifies NPR-B binding and the stem asks for the initiating receptor action.

item.vignette: A long-acting prodrug used in hypoparathyroidism undergoes gradual linker cleavage under physiologic conditions. The released peptide reproduces the biologically active N-terminal region of human parathyroid hormone and increases renal calcium reabsorption while promoting phosphate excretion.
item.lead_in: Which receptor is directly activated by the released peptide?

options.D: Vitamin D receptor

item.tested_construct: Continuous PTH(1-34) release and PTH1R activation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires distinguishing hormone replacement from calcium-sensing and vitamin-D pathways.

explanation.key_explanation: Palopegteriparatide is a prodrug that releases PTH(1-34). Released PTH(1-34) activates PTH1R, producing effects analogous to endogenous PTH on bone and kidney mineral handling.

distractor_explanations.A: CaSR senses extracellular calcium and is not activated by PTH(1-34).
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Released PTH(1-34) acts through PTH1R.
distractor_explanations.C: FGFR1 is not the direct receptor for PTH.
distractor_explanations.D: Active vitamin D is generated downstream of PTH action but the vitamin D receptor is not the released peptide's target.
distractor_explanations.E: Calcitonin receptors mediate a different calcium-regulatory hormone pathway.

explanation.educational_objective: Identify the receptor mediating physiologic hormone-replacement effects from a controlled-release prodrug.

sources.title: YORVIPATH- palopegteriparatide injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Current DailyMed label updated 2026-04-21; 12.1 and 12.3 checked 2026-09-08; section-specific revision date not guessed

second_answer_attack.resolution: PTH increases active vitamin-D synthesis, but the released PTH peptide itself directly activates PTH1R rather than VDR.

item.vignette: Two epithelial preparations are exposed to sotagliflozin. In proximal renal tubules, sodium-coupled glucose reabsorption decreases; in small-intestinal epithelium, sodium-coupled glucose absorption also decreases. The cardiovascular mechanism of benefit is not assumed from this experiment.
item.lead_in: Which transporter pair is directly inhibited?

options.D: NHE3 and SGLT2

item.tested_construct: Dual SGLT2/SGLT1 inhibition across kidney and intestine
item.difficulty_basis: Requires matching tissue localization of two sodium-glucose cotransporters while respecting uncertainty about cardiovascular benefit mechanism.

explanation.key_explanation: Sotagliflozin inhibits both SGLT2 and SGLT1. SGLT2 inhibition reduces renal glucose/sodium reabsorption, whereas SGLT1 inhibition reduces intestinal glucose/sodium absorption.

distractor_explanations.A: GLUT4 is an insulin-responsive facilitative transporter rather than the intestinal sodium-glucose cotransporter.
distractor_explanations.B: GLUT2 is facilitative and is not the second direct sotagliflozin target.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The paired renal and intestinal effects identify SGLT2 plus SGLT1 inhibition.
distractor_explanations.D: NHE3 is not a labeled sotagliflozin target.
distractor_explanations.E: Na+/K+-ATPase drives gradients but is not directly inhibited by sotagliflozin.

explanation.educational_objective: Use tissue-specific transport physiology to identify dual sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibition.

sources.title: INPEFA- sotagliflozin tablet
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.1 section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: SGLT1 participates in intestinal uptake, but GLUT2 is not the second labeled direct target; the renal effect identifies SGLT2.

author_qa.hidden_assumptions: PASS — cardiovascular benefit mechanism explicitly not inferred

item.vignette: An HIV-1 virion is incubated with the active moiety of fostemsavir before exposure to a CD4-positive target cell. Viral envelope gp120 remains present, but soluble CD4 binding to gp120 decreases and viral attachment is impaired. Reverse-transcriptase and integrase activities are unchanged in cell-free assays.
item.lead_in: Which direct interaction explains the antiviral effect?

options.A: Binding CCR5 to prevent coreceptor engagement
options.B: Inhibiting reverse transcriptase after viral entry
options.D: Binding gp120 and preventing its interaction with cellular CD4

item.difficulty_basis: Requires localizing inhibition to viral attachment rather than post-entry replication enzymes or host coreceptors.

explanation.key_explanation: Fostemsavir is a prodrug of temsavir. Temsavir binds HIV-1 gp120 and inhibits its interaction with cellular CD4, preventing attachment and also affecting gp120-dependent post-attachment entry steps.

distractor_explanations.A: CCR5 antagonism targets a host coreceptor, not gp120 directly.
distractor_explanations.B: Reverse transcriptase acts after entry and is unchanged in the assay.
distractor_explanations.C: Integrase acts after reverse transcription and is unchanged.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Reduced soluble-CD4 binding to gp120 directly identifies temsavir attachment inhibition.
distractor_explanations.E: Protease functions during virion maturation rather than initial attachment.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate direct viral-envelope attachment inhibition from host-coreceptor blockade and post-entry antiretroviral targets.

sources.title: RUKOBIA- fostemsavir extended-release tablet
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Mechanism text in current DailyMed 12.4 section carries this date; current label page checked 2026-09-08 and no newer mechanism date inferred from unrelated sections

second_answer_attack.resolution: CCR5 blockade also prevents entry, but the direct gp120 binding and reduced soluble-CD4 interaction uniquely identify temsavir's attachment mechanism.

item.vignette: A multidrug-resistant aerobic Gram-negative bacterium is grown under iron-limited conditions with cefiderocol. The drug forms a ferric-iron complex and is actively transported into the periplasm through bacterial siderophore uptake systems. Once in the periplasm, peptidoglycan synthesis is inhibited.
item.lead_in: Which mechanism best describes the antibiotic's combined uptake and lethal action?

options.A: Passive diffusion followed by inhibition of DNA gyrase
options.B: Porin-independent uptake followed by 30S ribosomal inhibition
options.C: Iron chelation that kills solely by starving the bacterium of iron
options.D: Siderophore uptake followed by inhibition of beta-lactamase enzymes
options.E: Siderophore-mediated periplasmic entry followed by binding to penicillin-binding proteins

item.tested_construct: Siderophore cephalosporin uptake plus PBP-mediated cell-wall inhibition
item.difficulty_basis: Requires separating the transport mechanism from the downstream beta-lactam target.

explanation.key_explanation: Cefiderocol functions as a siderophore, binds ferric iron, and exploits bacterial siderophore iron-uptake systems to reach the periplasm. It then binds PBPs and inhibits bacterial cell-wall biosynthesis.

distractor_explanations.A: The lethal target is not DNA gyrase and active siderophore uptake is central to entry.
distractor_explanations.B: The downstream target is PBPs rather than the 30S ribosome.
distractor_explanations.C: Iron binding facilitates uptake; bactericidal activity is due to PBP-mediated inhibition of cell-wall synthesis rather than simple iron starvation.
distractor_explanations.D: Cefiderocol may be stable to several beta-lactamases, but beta-lactamase inhibition is not its direct lethal target.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. The drug combines siderophore-mediated uptake with cephalosporin PBP inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Separate a drug-delivery strategy from the intracellular/periplasmic molecular target responsible for bacterial killing.

sources.title: FETROJA- cefiderocol for injection
sources.agency: Manufacturer prescribing information hosted by NLM DailyMed
sources.date_basis: Date encoded on current DailyMed 12.4 mechanism section; page checked 2026-09-08

second_answer_attack.resolution: Ferric-iron binding is real but serves active uptake; the label identifies PBP binding/cell-wall inhibition as the bactericidal mechanism.
